references.text: Isaiah 9:1-2 predicts that the people who walked in darkness will see a great light, a direct counterpart to the physical and spiritual blindness healed in John 9.
Isaiah 42:7 describes the Messiah's task of opening blind eyes, a prophecy fulfilled concretely when Jesus sends the man to Siloam to restore his sight.
Isaiah 35:5 promises that the blind will receive their sight again in messianic times, which happens immediately after the man washes himself in Siloam.
John 1:9 refers to Jesus as the true light that enlightens every person, a theme central to John 9 where Jesus is 'the light of the world' who gives sight to the blind.
In John 11:40, Jesus emphasizes that whoever believes will see God's glory, a parallel to the blind man who sees both physically and spiritually after obeying Jesus' command.
John 12:46 confirms that Jesus came as a light so that no one who believes should remain in darkness, directly linked to the healing of the blind man in chapter 9.
